stem: Two matched ventricular preparations have identical preload and contractility. The resistance of the vascular circuit is reduced in preparation X and left unchanged in preparation Y. The investigator measures the volume expelled per beat. Which of the following comparisons is expected?

options.text: Greater in X because the opposing load is higher
options.explanation: Greater ejection is expected, but not for the proposed reason. Reducing vascular resistance lowers the opposing load instead of making ejection mechanically more demanding.
options.label: A
options.misconception: Correctly predicts greater ejection but attributes it to higher opposition after resistance was reduced.

options.text: Lower in X because the opposing load is higher
options.explanation: Both the load and output predictions contradict the intervention. Reduced vascular resistance lowers afterload and supports a greater stroke volume at fixed contraction strength.
options.label: B
options.misconception: Reverses both the afterload change and its effect on ejection after circuit resistance falls.

options.text: Equal in X because the initial filling is equal
options.explanation: Equal preload does not guarantee equal stroke volume. Ejection also depends on afterload, which differs between the two circuits despite their matched starting conditions.
options.label: C
options.misconception: Assumes that equal preload guarantees equal stroke volume despite different afterloads.

options.text: Greater in X because the opposing load is lower
options.explanation: Lower circuit resistance reduces afterload. With the same preload and contractility, less opposition to ejection permits a larger stroke volume in preparation X.
options.label: D
options.misconception: No misconception: reducing afterload permits greater ejection at matched preload and contractility.

options.text: Lower in X because the opposing load is lower
options.explanation: The load change is described correctly, but its consequence is reversed. Lower afterload facilitates emptying rather than reducing the amount expelled under matched conditions.
options.label: E
options.misconception: Assumes that lower afterload reduces rather than facilitates ejection under matched conditions.

context: Learning objective: Predict a stroke-volume difference produced by altered resistance independently of preload or contractility. Lower circuit resistance reduces afterload. With the same preload and contractility, less opposition to ejection permits a larger stroke volume in preparation X.
